definitions.explanation: The track-and-field event in which the athlete swings a metal ball attached to a wire handle inside a throwing circle and releases it for maximum distance. One of the four throwing events in athletics, alongside shot put, discus, and javelin.

examples.japanese: ハンマー{投|な}げの{選手|せんしゅ}。
{彼|かれ}はハンマー{投|な}げで{金|きん}メダルを{取|と}った。
examples.english: He won a gold medal in the hammer throw.

examples.japanese: ハンマー{投|な}げは{投擲|とうてき}{種目|しゅもく}の{一|ひと}つである。
examples.english: The hammer throw is one of the throwing events.

examples.japanese: {室伏広治|むろふしこうじ}{選手|せんしゅ}は、アテネオリンピックのハンマー{投|な}げで{金|きん}メダルを{獲得|かくとく}した。
examples.english: Athlete Koji Murofushi won the gold medal in the hammer throw at the Athens Olympics.

notes:
Composed of the loanword ハンマー (hammer) and the nominalized verb stem {投|な}げ (throwing, from {投|な}げる "to throw"). Refers only to the athletic event, not to throwing an actual hammer.

USAGE:
Used almost exclusively as the name of the sport. The person who competes is a ハンマー{投|な}げ{選手|せんしゅ}. The implement itself is called a ハンマー, though it is actually a metal ball on a wire.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ハンマー{投|な}げの{選手|せんしゅ}: hammer thrower
- ハンマー{投|な}げの{記録|きろく}: hammer throw record
- ハンマー{投|な}げで{優勝|ゆうしょう}する: to win the hammer throw
- ハンマー{投|な}げの{決勝|けっしょう}: the hammer throw final

RELATED EVENTS:
- {砲丸投|ほうがんな}げ: shot put
- {円盤投|えんばんな}げ: discus throw
- やり{投|な}げ: javelin throw

All four of these {投擲種目|とうてきしゅもく} (throwing events) follow the same {〜投|な}げ naming pattern, using a nominalized form of {投|な}げる.
